record_type_quote: We report a replication of Boutonnet and Lupyan’s (2015) study of the effects of linguistic labelling on perceptual performance.

targets.title: Words jump-start vision: A label advantage in object recognition.
targets.evidence_quote: Given the controversy over this claim and the need for replication of key findings, we attempted to replicate Boutonnet and Lupyan (2015).
targets.outcome_quote: To summarize, our close and pre-registered replication of Boutonnet & Lupyan (2015) yielded consistent behavioral results but ERP patterns that were not only inconsistent but actually suggest that the beneficial effect of labels vs. sounds on judgments of matching and mismatching visual images was occurring at the semantic (N4) stage rather than an earlier perceptual (P1/P2) stage of processing.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors summarize the replication as consistent behavioral results with inconsistent ERP patterns, expressly contrasting the original findings.

reasoning: New participants re-test the published experiment. The discussion gives a summary verdict covering both consistent behavior and inconsistent ERP findings.
